label: LTX-2.5 distilled (text / keyframes to video + audio)

capabilities._note: duration: predict. LTX 2.4+ has a duration head: `dur: model` shots get ComfyUI's ModelPatchLoader (the preset's duration_head file, from models/model_patches) + LTXVDurationPredictor, whose num_frames (8k+1) drives every length input of the graph. The build writes an estimate (the dialogue's `dur: auto` length, else the preset's default_seconds); without the weights installed the take renders that estimate and says so.

template._note: LTX-2 renders 8k+1 frames (9, 17, ..., 97, ...). This workflow is two-stage: a base pass at half size, then the x2 latent upsampler and a refine pass, so the output must be a multiple of 64 (the base latent needs 32). Sizes that aren't legal are snapped down, then shrunk under 1 MP / 1536 on the long side. The frame rate is the series config's. LTX-2 handles about 20 s per shot.

recipe._note: Subjects are written in words from the series config's `design`, the location from its `description`; when the shot's refs are on disk AND the ingredients IC-LoRA is installed they are ALSO shown on a reference sheet (reference_sheet below), which is decided at queue time, never at build time, so a shotlist is what it always was. Optional shot keyframes: shot:<id>:first conditions frame 0 (LTXVImgToVideoInplace), shot:<id>:last the final frame (LTXVAddGuide). A shot with neither renders text-to-video. LTX-2 makes the soundtrack with the picture and takes no voice sample or recording, so clone / dub / dub_keep_foley shots render with generate and say so.

policy_fallback.why: LTX-2 generates sound with the picture and takes no voice sample or recording

reference_sheet._note: The ltx2_ingredients sheet, on LTX-2.5: one panel per element, characters first (the face panel of a 4-panel sheet on a single-character close-up, else the three-quarter body panel), then props and vehicles, then the location plate, tiled on black at the render size (comfy_nodes/h3_refsheet.py, through targets/video/ltx2_ingredients/sheet.py). Unlike ltx2_ingredients, every panel is OPTIONAL here: a missing file drops that element from the sheet, and a shot left with none renders exactly as ltx2 always did. `min_frames` is the model card's floor for the looped reference video (121 frames): the guide can't be longer than the clip, so a shorter shot only earns a note that identity may weaken. `stages` are the sampling stages that get the guide (1 = the base pass, 2 = the refine pass). `strength` is the model card's default (the weights ship pre-scaled).

sampling._note: Which sampling schedule each transformer wants, chosen at queue time from the file the job loads (`match`, globs on the file name). `distilled` is the workflow's own and patches nothing: a fixed 8-step base ManualSigmas plus a 3-step refine at cfg 1, so `steps` is recorded, not used. `dev` is the quality profile: patch_graph swaps the base stage's ManualSigmas for an LTXVScheduler at the shot's `steps` and sets both stages' guiders and samplers. Where the numbers come from: ComfyUI's LTX-2 dev templates (video_ltx2_t2v.json runs the dev checkpoint through LTXVScheduler 20 / 2.05 / 0.95 / stretch / terminal 0.1 with CFGGuider 4 on the base stage and 1 on the refine), the LTX-2.5 model card (the distilled file is the fixed 8-step cfg-1 one; dev takes variable steps and guidance), and the live 97-frame runs of one shot at 768x512 on 2026-09-19 recorded in docs/API.md 'LTX-2.5: the quality profile and ingredients references'. Two of those settings are in no template and were decided there: `scheduler.latent` (the base stage's own video latent goes into LTXVScheduler, so its shift follows the shot's token count; without it the node assumes 4096 tokens, shifts as if the latent were far bigger, and the clip comes out soft and painterly) and `euler_ancestral` (plain `euler`, which the LTX-2 dev templates use on a checkpoint carrying the distilled LoRA, came out soft with mangled hands on every cfg tried; ancestral is also what the distilled 2.5 workflow uses). The refine block is the workflow's own refine, written out so the take records it.

with_sheet._note: What changes when the same shot also draws a reference sheet. The IC-LoRA reads the sheet as frames IN CONTEXT with the clip, and an ancestral sampler re-injects noise over those frames too: on the dev transformer at real guidance that speckles the figure and makes it come and go (three live runs). Plain euler holds it. Guidance also has to come down — ComfyUI's ingredients graph advises cfg near 1, and the dev model needs more than 1 to resolve at all, so 3.0 is the live compromise. Even so, distilled + sheet is the cleaner picture of the two: the take says so.

size_hints.keyframe: the render size (any size works: it is resized to the frame)

binding._note: The workflow is ComfyUI's LTX-2.5 image-to-video template (a subgraph, flattened by h3jobs.ui_to_api). Every value is patched straight into a widget: there is no loader node, so a text-only shot needs no custom node beyond H3SaveShot, which takes the place of CreateVideo/SaveVideo. The prompt enhancer (TextGenerateLTX2Prompt) is never used: the prompt goes into the positive CLIPTextEncode, and prune drops the enhancer with everything else the saver doesn't need.

duration_predictor._note: For `dur: model` (capabilities.duration): h3jobs.graph_for adds ModelPatchLoader + LTXVDurationPredictor, reading the model and positive conditioning that feed these inputs, and links its num_frames into every `length` widget above.

models._note: The family each model param must be (targets/modelid.py): names first, then the file's header (LTX files carry model_version; 2.5's transformer also has keyframes_abs_pos_embedding and no video feed-forward biases). The 2.3 and 2.5 upscalers share every tensor and have no metadata: only the name tells them apart. duration_head is a preset value, not a binding widget: ModelPatchLoader reads it from models/model_patches; quality_model and reference_lora are neither — they have no preset value and no widget of their own, only a `default`, so readiness (targets.wanted_files) and `h3.py targets` can say whether the two extras are installed. Tiers (docs/API.md): the duration head, the dev transformer and the ingredients IC-LoRA are optional (without one, only its feature is off); everything else is required. No base: the preset is already the distilled model with the workflow's fixed 8 + 3 step schedule, and the dev model needs another schedule (recipe.sampling), so a substitute must say `distilled` like the wanted file (`keep`).

nodes._note: Node classes beyond the workflow's own: the keyframe conditioning patch_graph adds (ComfyUI core), the duration predictor `dur: model` adds, the reference sheet adds (ComfyUI-LTXVideo's two IC-LoRA nodes, as ComfyUI's LTX-2.5 ingredients template wires them, plus two core image nodes) and the quality profile adds (LTXVScheduler, core). All four extras are optional: without their nodes only that feature is off.

presets._note: LTX-2.5 22B distilled (int8): a fixed 8-step base schedule plus a 3-step refine (the workflow's ManualSigmas; `steps` is recorded, not patched). The final is the workflow's 768x512 unless the series config sets a size; the proxy is 448x256. Both use the same model: the distilled model is already fast. The negative prompt is the IC-LoRA model card's suggestion plus the artefacts a review cut can't use; the template's own ('pc game, ..., cartoon, childish') would fight a cartoon series' look. For `dur: model` (capabilities): duration_head is the LTX-2.5 duration head in models/model_patches (not in the shotlist's defaults; checked at queue time), default_seconds the estimate of a silent shot, min_seconds/max_seconds the predictor's range when the script gives none.

final.negative: worst quality, inconsistent motion, blurry, jittery, distorted, flickering, morphing, extra limbs, watermark, subtitles

proxy.negative: worst quality, inconsistent motion, blurry, jittery, distorted, flickering, morphing, extra limbs, watermark, subtitles

downloads._note: Where to get each file this target names (docs/API.md 'Downloads'). A url is only given when a trustworthy record has it: a ComfyUI template's or saved workflow's properties.models entry, ComfyUI-Manager's model list, or (the ingredients IC-LoRA, which neither lists) the file listing of the model's own Hugging Face repo, read from the Hub API; `source` says which. Otherwise url is null and source says what to search for. Never a guessed URL.
